Two levels of comparability: Standards and Assessments

Uneven performance standards across states has led numerous
policy makers and researchers to argue that interstate comparisons
of quality are basically meaningless [Linn, 2001].
The Common Core State Standards and the two multi-state
assessment consortia (PARCC and SBAC) represent moves toward
greater cross state comparability.
The data can tell a thousand stories: What stories are likely to
emerge.

The Assessment Consortium

As part of the Race to the Top initiative, unprecedented resources
have been made available for the development of next generation
assessments.
More than $350 million was made available with two proposals
receiving awards: Partnership for Assessment of Readiness for
College and Careers (PARCC) and the Smarter Balanced
Assessment Consortium (SBAC).
PARCC: 26 states serving more than 30 million students. SBAC: 31
states serving more than 20 million students.
Both consortia are currently in active development/planning in
preparation for assessment use in 2014-2015.

Student Growth

As the PARCC title suggests, career and college readiness has
become the new proficiency.
Recent ESEA re-authorization blueprints reference all students
being career and college ready by 2020.
Both PARCC and SBAC promote the idea of growth toward the
standard of career and college readiness.

Student Growth and Value-Added

With RttT, state efforts toward utilizing student growth have become
increasingly rapid.
States receiving RttT funding are required to use student
assessment results, when available, as part of educator evaluation.
Many states not receiving RttT funding passed legislation requiring
the same.
Student growth is now a primary part of many states’ accountability
initiatives, both personnel (e.g., teacher or principal) and institutional
(e.g., school or district)
Value-added methodologies have been used for more than a decade
toward this end.
Integrating value-added and growth-to-career and college readiness
is the next big challenge.
